correctness.rationale: For rank at most one, factorization through the two-dimensional free lattice over a one-dimensional real space makes the extension finite rank. For rank two on a real two-space, finite-dimensional FBL(p)[G] is C(S_G*) under an equivalent lattice norm, enabling disjoint continuous bumps. If supports lie in the neighborhood where dual evaluation at x exceeds 1-eta, the defining p-norm is at most (1-eta)^(-1); the p=infinity endpoint is immediate. The bumps are weakly null and every compact map sends them to zero in norm. Evaluating the induced maps at norm-one dual functionals converging to a norming functional gives lower bound (1-eta)||S||. Restricting an arbitrary rank-at-least-two inducing map to norming two-spaces transfers the bound. The reverse bound follows from ||F_p(T)||=||T||. No finite experiments or unproved infinite enumeration are used.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected 2022/2024 Oikhberg–Taylor–Tradacete–Troitsky work develops induced free-lattice maps, finite-dimensional C(S) models and weak compactness considerations but does not state the full essential-norm rank dichotomy. Explicit searches for synonymous compactness, distances, approximation numbers, and weighted-composition reformulations identified no dominating theorem. The known weighted-composition profile on ordinary C(K) concerns a different norm; lattice isomorphism rather than isometry does not transfer the exact equality. Novelty is contingent on the documented residual literature risks.
residual_risks: Exact essential-norm formula may have appeared as an implicit corollary or differently named weighted-composition theorem not found in indexed searches.
The broader literature on essential norms of composition operators on equivalent continuous-function renormings is too large for exhaustive manual verification.
The 2023 complex free-lattice article was checked for context but the claim is deliberately restricted to real lattices.

value.rationale: The complete rank threshold and exact essential distance uniformly across all real Banach spaces and p in [1,infinity] is a natural quantitative structural classification. Unlike a simple corollary of isomorphic C(K) representation, the numerical constant is sharp under the non-supremum FBL(p) norm. It implies all approximation numbers flatten at ||T|| and establishes a striking norm discontinuity at rank-one limits; the formula is not simply a renamed definition or isolated small-parameter calculation.
